claim: Pre-follicular mouse oogenesis takes place in germline cysts.
source: Recent studies show that pre-follicular mouse oogenesis takes place in germline cysts, highly conserved groups of oogonial cells connected by intercellular bridges that develop as nurse cells as well as an oocyte.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of recent studies.

claim: Germline cysts are highly conserved groups of oogonial cells connected by intercellular bridges.
source: Recent studies show that pre-follicular mouse oogenesis takes place in germline cysts, highly conserved groups of oogonial cells connected by intercellular bridges that develop as nurse cells as well as an oocyte.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about germline cysts provided in the abstract.

claim: Female germline cysts acquire cytoskeletal polarity.
source: Long studied in Drosophila and insect gametogenesis, female germline cysts acquire cytoskeletal polarity and traffic centrosomes and organelles between nurse cells and the oocyte to form the Balbiani body, a conserved marker of polarity.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding from studies in Drosophila and insects.

claim: Female germline cysts traffic centrosomes and organelles between nurse cells and the oocyte to form the Balbiani body.
source: Long studied in Drosophila and insect gametogenesis, female germline cysts acquire cytoskeletal polarity and traffic centrosomes and organelles between nurse cells and the oocyte to form the Balbiani body, a conserved marker of polarity.
evidence: This describes a specific biological process observed in germline cysts.

claim: The Balbiani body is a conserved marker of polarity.
source: Long studied in Drosophila and insect gametogenesis, female germline cysts acquire cytoskeletal polarity and traffic centrosomes and organelles between nurse cells and the oocyte to form the Balbiani body, a conserved marker of polarity.
evidence: This characterizes the Balbiani body based on comparative studies.

claim: Mouse oocyte development is supported by dynamic, cell-specific programs of germline gene expression.
source: Mouse oocyte development and nurse cell dumping are supported by dynamic, cell-specific programs of germline gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as a finding about mouse oogenesis.

claim: Mouse nurse cell dumping is supported by dynamic, cell-specific programs of germline gene expression.
source: Mouse oocyte development and nurse cell dumping are supported by dynamic, cell-specific programs of germline gene expression.
evidence: This describes a mechanism supporting nurse cell function.

claim: High levels of perinatal germ cell death in mice primarily result from programmed nurse cell turnover after transfer rather than defective oocyte production.
source: High levels of perinatal germ cell death in this species primarily result from programmed nurse cell turnover after transfer rather than defective oocyte production.
evidence: This provides an explanation for a previously observed phenomenon.

claim: Early oogenesis mechanisms are strikingly conserved between distant animal groups.
source: The striking evolutionary conservation of early oogenesis mechanisms between distant animal groups strongly suggests that gametogenesis and early embryonic development in vertebrates and invertebrates share even more in common than currently believed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparative analysis.

claim: Gametogenesis and early embryonic development in vertebrates and invertebrates share more in common than currently believed.
source: The striking evolutionary conservation of early oogenesis mechanisms between distant animal groups strongly suggests that gametogenesis and early embryonic development in vertebrates and invertebrates share even more in common than currently believed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed conservation of mechanisms.

claim: The mature oocyte contains essentially all the molecules of the zygote.
source: The mature oocyte from which a child arises contains essentially all the molecules of the zygote, as the sperm provides almost nothing that lasts except a set of chromosomes and a centriole.
evidence: This is a statement about the maternal contribution to the zygote.

claim: The sperm provides almost nothing that lasts except a set of chromosomes and a centriole.
source: The mature oocyte from which a child arises contains essentially all the molecules of the zygote, as the sperm provides almost nothing that lasts except a set of chromosomes and a centriole.
evidence: This describes the limited paternal contribution to the zygote.

claim: The germline cyst is a multicellular structure that appears to have originated at the dawn of animal evolution.
source: It has recently become clear that the oocyte-forming events that begin during the mother's fetal development take place within a highly stereotyped cellular environment - the germline cyst - a multicellular structure that appears to have originated at the dawn of animal evolution, but which for years was studied mostly in Drosophila and other insects.
evidence: This is a statement about the evolutionary origin of germline cysts.

claim: Germline cysts were studied mostly in Drosophila and other insects for years.
source: It has recently become clear that the oocyte-forming events that begin during the mother's fetal development take place within a highly stereotyped cellular environment - the germline cyst - a multicellular structure that appears to have originated at the dawn of animal evolution, but which for years was studied mostly in Drosophila and other insects.
evidence: This is a historical statement about research focus.

claim: Cysts support oocyte production by defining nurse cells as well as oocytes.
source: How cysts support Drosophila and mammalian oocyte production by defining nurse cells (NCs) as well as oocytes, mediating organelle transfer, establishing the oocyte-specific organellar aggregate known as the Balbiani body (Bb) and possibly contributing to successful embryonic development will be reviewed here.
evidence: This describes one of the functions of cysts.

claim: Cysts mediate organelle transfer.
source: How cysts support Drosophila and mammalian oocyte production by defining nurse cells (NCs) as well as oocytes, mediating organelle transfer, establishing the oocyte-specific organellar aggregate known as the Balbiani body (Bb) and possibly contributing to successful embryonic development will be reviewed here.
evidence: This describes a mechanism by which cysts support oocyte production.

claim: Cysts establish the oocyte-specific organellar aggregate known as the Balbiani body.
source: How cysts support Drosophila and mammalian oocyte production by defining nurse cells (NCs) as well as oocytes, mediating organelle transfer, establishing the oocyte-specific organellar aggregate known as the Balbiani body (Bb) and possibly contributing to successful embryonic development will be reviewed here.
evidence: This describes a role of cysts in establishing the Balbiani body.

claim: Cysts possibly contribute to successful embryonic development.
source: How cysts support Drosophila and mammalian oocyte production by defining nurse cells (NCs) as well as oocytes, mediating organelle transfer, establishing the oocyte-specific organellar aggregate known as the Balbiani body (Bb) and possibly contributing to successful embryonic development will be reviewed here.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential function of cysts.

claim: Germ cells are initially specified by Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) signaling during early gastrulation.
source: Germ cells are initially specified by Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) signaling during early gastrulation (Lawson et al., 1999; review Monsivais et al., 2017), after which they reprogram epigenetic marks (Sanford et al., 1987; Reik and Surani, 2015; Nicholls and Page, 2021; Saitou and Hayashi, 2021) and migrate to the gonads to initiate gamete production.
evidence: This is supported by cited research on germ cell specification.

claim: Germ cells reprogram epigenetic marks after specification.
source: Germ cells are initially specified by Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) signaling during early gastrulation (Lawson et al., 1999; review Monsivais et al., 2017), after which they reprogram epigenetic marks (Sanford et al., 1987; Reik and Surani, 2015; Nicholls and Page, 2021; Saitou and Hayashi, 2021) and migrate to the gonads to initiate gamete production.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations on epigenetic reprogramming.

claim: Germ cells migrate to the gonads to initiate gamete production.
source: Germ cells are initially specified by Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) signaling during early gastrulation (Lawson et al., 1999; review Monsivais et al., 2017), after which they reprogram epigenetic marks (Sanford et al., 1987; Reik and Surani, 2015; Nicholls and Page, 2021; Saitou and Hayashi, 2021) and migrate to the gonads to initiate gamete production.
evidence: This describes a known developmental process.

claim: A large fraction of mammalian female germ cells die rather than forming oocytes, especially during perinatal stages.
source: A perplexing feature of mammalian oogenesis has been the large fraction of female germ cells that die rather than forming oocytes, especially during perinatal stages, suggesting that most germ cells are defective in some way and need to be culled (discussed in Tilly, 2001; Grive, 2020).
evidence: This is an observed phenomenon discussed in the cited literature.

claim: The large fraction of germ cell death suggests that most germ cells are defective in some way and need to be culled.
source: A perplexing feature of mammalian oogenesis has been the large fraction of female germ cells that die rather than forming oocytes, especially during perinatal stages, suggesting that most germ cells are defective in some way and need to be culled (discussed in Tilly, 2001; Grive, 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the observed germ cell death.

claim: Widely conserved core genes (such as Vasa, Nanos, Piwi, Tudor, etc.) underlying the biology of all animal germ cells were identified through studies in invertebrate models.
source: Widely conserved core genes (such as Vasa, Nanos, Piwi, Tudor, etc.) underlying the biology of all animal germ cells were identified (Fierro-Constaín et al., 2017; Sundby et al., 2021; Mercer et al., 2021) as well as hundreds of other maternally expressed genes, both conserved and more rapidly evolving, that contribute to oocyte production and early embryogenesis (Elis et al., 2018; Whittle and Extavour, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited research identifying conserved germ cell genes.

claim: Hundreds of other maternally expressed genes, both conserved and more rapidly evolving, contribute to oocyte production and early embryogenesis.
source: Widely conserved core genes (such as Vasa, Nanos, Piwi, Tudor, etc.) underlying the biology of all animal germ cells were identified (Fierro-Constaín et al., 2017; Sundby et al., 2021; Mercer et al., 2021) as well as hundreds of other maternally expressed genes, both conserved and more rapidly evolving, that contribute to oocyte production and early embryogenesis (Elis et al., 2018; Whittle and Extavour, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited research on maternal gene expression.

claim: Germline cysts are groups of germ cells interconnected by distinctive intercellular bridges.
source: Germline cysts are groups of germ cells interconnected by distinctive intercellular bridges (IBs) that are generated using synchronous mitotic divisions with incomplete cytokinesis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Germline cysts are generated using synchronous mitotic divisions with incomplete cytokinesis.
source: Germline cysts are groups of germ cells interconnected by distinctive intercellular bridges (IBs) that are generated using synchronous mitotic divisions with incomplete cytokinesis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of cyst formation, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In Drosophila and other insects, the intercellular bridges later acquire additional proteins and actin to support their expansion into large 'ring canals'.
source: In Drosophila and other insects, the IBs later acquire additional proteins and actin to support their expansion into large 'ring canals' (Robinson and Cooley, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing ring canal formation.

claim: Cysts produced by incomplete cytokinesis appear to be nearly universal in male gametogenesis.
source: Cysts produced in this manner appear to be nearly universal in male gametogenesis and are found during early steps of oocyte production in diverse major animal groups including higher insects with complete metamorphosis where they persist longer and are most easily studied (Giardina, 1901; Wilson, 1925; Büning, 1994; Matova and Cooley, 2001; Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a generalization based on observations across animal groups, supported by citations.

claim: Cysts are found during early steps of oocyte production in diverse major animal groups including higher insects with complete metamorphosis.
source: Cysts produced in this manner appear to be nearly universal in male gametogenesis and are found during early steps of oocyte production in diverse major animal groups including higher insects with complete metamorphosis where they persist longer and are most easily studied (Giardina, 1901; Wilson, 1925; Büning, 1994; Matova and Cooley, 2001; Lu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by historical and recent citations on cyst occurrence.

claim: Many invertebrates use interconnected syncytial cellular structures within their gonad built using a variant of the cyst formation program.
source: Many other invertebrates use interconnected syncytial cellular structures within their gonad for similar purposes that are built using a variant of the cyst formation program (Swiatek et al., 2009; Seidel et al., 2018; Świątek and Urbisz, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing variations in cyst formation.

claim: Cyst utilization has not been detected in females from some phylogenetic groups, a condition termed 'panoistic.'
source: However, cyst utilization has not been detected in females from some phylogenetic groups, a condition termed 'panoistic.'
evidence: This defines a term for species lacking cysts.

claim: Many panoistic groups appear to have secondarily lost cyst production during evolution.
source: While in some panoistic species cyst formation early in development may have been overlooked, many such groups appear to have secondarily lost cyst production during evolution (Büning, 1994).
evidence: This is an evolutionary inference supported by a citation.

claim: A germline stem cell (GSC) divides asymmetrically to generate a cystoblast (CB).
source: A germline stem cell (GSC) divides asymmetrically to generate a cystoblast (CB).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: The cystoblast divides with incomplete cytokinesis to generate a two-cell cyst with an intercellular bridge.
source: The CB divides with incomplete cytokinesis to generate a two-cell cyst (2CC) with an intercellular bridge (IB).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Three more cycles of rapid, synchronous, incomplete cyst divisions follow to generate 4CC, 8CC, and 16CC.
source: Three more cycles of rapid, synchronous, incomplete cyst divisions follow to generate 4CC, 8CC, and 16CC.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: One cell in the 16-cell cyst differentiates into an oocyte while the other cells become nurse cells.
source: One cell (dark) differentiates into an oocyte (O) while the other cells (gray) become nurse cells (NCs).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Drosophila oogenesis begins in the germarium at the tip of each ovariole that houses germline stem cells.
source: Drosophila oogenesis begins in the germarium (Figure 1B) at the tip of each ovariole that houses germline stem cells (GSCs).
evidence: This describes the anatomical location where oogenesis begins, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The fusome is a microtubule-dependent organelle that grows with each successive mitotic division.
source: Cysts then participate in all the key developmental processes of early oogenesis including meiosis, oocyte specification, patterning, and Bb formation. Cysts influence these events by first acquiring an asymmetric cytoskeletal structure (Figure 1C–F) known as 'the fusome' (meaning 'spindle derived'). This microtubule (MT)-dependent organelle grows with each successive mitotic division, interconnects all cyst cells, mediates germ cell cycle synchronization, and is essential for oocyte specification (Telfer, 1975; Lin et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1C-F.

claim: The fusome interconnects all cyst cells.
source: This microtubule (MT)-dependent organelle grows with each successive mitotic division, interconnects all cyst cells, mediates germ cell cycle synchronization, and is essential for oocyte specification (Telfer, 1975; Lin et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes a structural feature of the fusome, supported by citations.

claim: The fusome mediates germ cell cycle synchronization.
source: This microtubule (MT)-dependent organelle grows with each successive mitotic division, interconnects all cyst cells, mediates germ cell cycle synchronization, and is essential for oocyte specification (Telfer, 1975; Lin et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes a functional role of the fusome, supported by citations.

claim: The fusome is essential for oocyte specification.
source: This microtubule (MT)-dependent organelle grows with each successive mitotic division, interconnects all cyst cells, mediates germ cell cycle synchronization, and is essential for oocyte specification (Telfer, 1975; Lin et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes a critical function of the fusome, supported by citations.

claim: All cyst-forming divisions are asymmetric, with the older cell inheriting a larger amount of fusome than its daughter.
source: All cyst-forming divisions are asymmetric, with the older cell inheriting a larger amount of fusome than its daughter (Figure 1C; de Cuevas and Spradling, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Central spindle microtubules that initially arrest cytokinesis appear to be incorporated into the fusome in a polarized manner.
source: The central spindle MTs that initially arrest cytokinesis appear to be incorporated into the fusome in a polarized manner, allowing directed movement of cellular components toward the future oocyte to begin shortly after cyst completion (reviews: Spradling et al., 1997; Milas and Telley, 2022).
evidence: This is a mechanistic description supported by review citations.

claim: Fusome microtubules are stabilized by tubulin acetylation, the spectraplakin protein Shot, and the CAMSAP protein Patronin.
source: Fusome MTs are stabilized by tubulin acetylation, the spectraplakin protein Shot, and the CAMSAP protein Patronin (Röper and Brown, 2004; Nashchekin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing MT stabilization mechanisms.

claim: Fusome MT minus ends orient toward the older fusome segment as new segments attach following each cyst division cycle.
source: A simple and sufficient model is that fusome MT minus ends orient toward the older fusome segment as new segments attach following each cyst division cycle to generate a finished fusome-associated network capable of transporting cargos from any cyst cell toward the initial cell (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a model proposed to explain fusome polarity, illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: More than 20 fusome proteins have been identified.
source: The detailed molecular organization of fusome components remains incompletely understood, and some of the more than 20 identified fusome proteins change as cysts develop in the germarium (Lighthouse et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation identifying fusome proteins.

claim: Fusome-specific isoforms of Adducin-like proteins produced by the hu-li tai shao (hts) gene and alpha-Spectrin are essential to prevent fusome dispersal.
source: Fusome-specific isoforms of several Adducin-like proteins produced by the hu-li tai shao (hts) gene (Petrella et al., 2007) and alpha-Spectrin are essential to prevent fusome dispersal, suggesting that these proteins play different roles in this non-membrane bound organelle than they do when associated with plasma membranes (de Cuevas et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing protein functions.

claim: The SCF complex in the fusome controls CycA and CycE turnover and promotes the fusome's ability to regulate germ cell cycles.
source: The presence of the Skp, Cullin, F-box containing (SCF) complex in the fusome controlling CycA and CycE turnover promotes the fusome's ability to regulate germ cell cycles (Lilly et al., 2000; Ohlmeyer and Schüpbach, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the SCF complex function.

claim: Fusome-associated ER proteins and vesicles provide ER connectivity between all cyst cells.
source: Finally, fusome-associated Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) proteins and vesicles provide ER connectivity between all cyst cells (Figure 1E; Snapp et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: Following four rounds of cyst-forming mitotic divisions, meiotic entry takes place.
source: Following four rounds of cyst-forming mitotic divisions, meiotic entry takes place, for which cyst cells have already been preparing their chromosomes (Christophorou et al., 2013; Rubin et al., 2016; Gyuricza et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the timing of meiotic entry, supported by citations.

claim: One cell is elaborated as the oocyte based on asymmetric fusome-mediated transfer from the other 15 cyst cells of RNAs and likely other materials.
source: As meiotic prophase ensues, one cell is elaborated as the oocyte based on asymmetric fusome-mediated transfer from the other 15 cyst cells of RNAs, and likely other materials (see Hinnant et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of oocyte specification, supported by a citation.

claim: Nurse cells protect the oocyte by producing piRNAs.
source: NCs protect the oocyte by producing piRNAs (Guzzardo et al., 2013; Wang and Lin, 2021), promote oocyte growth and help to establish oocyte polarity and developmental patterning (review: Milas and Telley, 2022).
evidence: This describes a protective function of nurse cells, supported by citations.

claim: Nurse cells promote oocyte growth.
source: NCs protect the oocyte by producing piRNAs (Guzzardo et al., 2013; Wang and Lin, 2021), promote oocyte growth and help to establish oocyte polarity and developmental patterning (review: Milas and Telley, 2022).
evidence: This describes a function of nurse cells, supported by a review citation.

claim: Nurse cells help to establish oocyte polarity and developmental patterning.
source: NCs protect the oocyte by producing piRNAs (Guzzardo et al., 2013; Wang and Lin, 2021), promote oocyte growth and help to establish oocyte polarity and developmental patterning (review: Milas and Telley, 2022).
evidence: This describes a developmental function of nurse cells, supported by a review citation.

claim: Somatic cells provide vital support to developing germ cells throughout the germarium, often in response to germ cell EGF and Notch signals.
source: Somatic cells provide vital support to the developing germ cells throughout the germarium, often in response to germ cell Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF) and Notch signals.
evidence: This describes somatic cell functions in the germarium.

claim: Mutations or treatments that disrupt cyst structure, the fusome, or MT-dependent transfer generate mostly nurse cells, fail to produce normal oocytes, and cause female sterility.
source: Mutations or treatments that disrupt cyst structure, the fusome, or MT-dependent transfer generate mostly NCs, fail to produce normal oocytes, and are female sterile (Koch and Spitzer, 1983; Yue and Spradling, 1992; Mach and Lehmann, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing genetic studies.

claim: Production of a viable Drosophila oocyte without a cyst and NC transfer has never been documented.
source: Indeed production of a viable Drosophila oocyte without a cyst and NC transfer has never been documented (Schüpbach and Wieschaus, 1991; de Cuevas et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a negative result supported by citations.

claim: A cyst of 2n cells produces only 1 oocyte and 2n–1 nurse cells ('the 2n rule').
source: In every species, the number of oocytes and NCs produced per cyst represents a fundamental parameter of female gamete development. Generally, a cyst of 2n cells produces only 1 oocyte and 2n–1 NCs ('the 2n rule').
evidence: This describes a general rule observed across species.

claim: Production of more oocytes is usually associated with the fragmentation of the initial cyst into smaller cysts that then each follow the 2n rule.
source: Production of more oocytes is usually associated with the fragmentation of the initial cyst into smaller cysts that then each follow the 2n rule (Figure 1G; see Yamauchi and Yoshitake, 1982).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1G.

claim: Evidence that developing mammalian male and female germ cells become connected by intercellular bridges was found beginning in the 1950s using electron microscopy.
source: Evidence that developing mammalian male and female germ cells become connected by IBs was found beginning in the 1950s using electron microscopy (Burgos and Fawcett, 1955; review, Gondos, 1973), and similar findings were reported in Xenopus (al-Mukhtar and al-Mukhtar and Webb, 1971; Coggins, 1973).
evidence: This is a historical statement supported by citations.

claim: Similar findings of intercellular bridges were reported in Xenopus.
source: Evidence that developing mammalian male and female germ cells become connected by IBs was found beginning in the 1950s using electron microscopy (Burgos and Fawcett, 1955; review, Gondos, 1973), and similar findings were reported in Xenopus (al-Mukhtar and al-Mukhtar and Webb, 1971; Coggins, 1973).
evidence: This is supported by citations on Xenopus germ cells.

claim: Mouse primordial germ cells undergo synchronized mitotic divisions to generate cell clusters up to 32 cells and preferentially containing 2n cells.
source: Mouse primordial germ cells were eventually shown to undergo synchronized mitotic divisions to generate cell clusters up to 32 cells and preferentially containing 2n cells (Figure 1C; Pepling and Spradling, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and referenced in Figure 1C.

claim: The cyst mechanism is conserved in mice based on comparisons of Drosophila, Xenopus, and mouse early germ cells.
source: The authors concluded that the cyst mechanism was conserved in mice based on comparisons of Drosophila, Xenopus, and mouse early germ cells (review: Pepling et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparative analysis, supported by a review citation.

claim: Xenopus oogonia develop in 16 cell cysts interconnected much like in Drosophila.
source: Xenopus oogonia were found to develop in 16 cell cysts (Kloc et al., 2004a) interconnected much like in Drosophila.
evidence: This is supported by a citation on Xenopus oogenesis.

claim: In Xenopus, all 16 cyst cells become oocytes due to the rarity of apoptotic germ cells.
source: However, due to the rarity of apoptotic germ cells, Kloc et al., 2004a concluded that all 16 cyst cells become oocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion from a cited study on Xenopus.

claim: In mouse and Drosophila, nurse cells do not turn over primarily by apoptosis.
source: We now know that in mouse and Drosophila, NCs do not turn over primarily by apoptosis.
evidence: This is a statement of current knowledge contrasting with earlier assumptions.

claim: Ovarian germline cysts containing up to 32 cells were discovered in the fish Medaka.
source: Ovarian germline cysts containing up to 32 cells were subsequently discovered in the fish Medaka (Nakamura et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation on Medaka oogenesis.

claim: Medaka ovaries contain 'germinal cradles' tipped with GSCs whose daughters immediately enter the cyst formation program, much like a Drosophila germarium.
source: Medaka ovaries contain 'germinal cradles' tipped with GSCs whose daughters immediately enter the cyst formation program, much like a Drosophila germarium.
evidence: This describes a structural similarity between Medaka and Drosophila.

claim: Medaka ovarian cysts form by 3–5 rounds of synchronous divisions, persist for a period of time, undergo some cell death, and produce oocytes in follicles.
source: Medaka ovarian cysts form by 3–5 rounds of synchronous divisions, persist for a period to time, undergo some cell death, and produce oocytes in follicles (Nakamura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing Medaka cyst development.

claim: Similar cysts to those in Medaka were observed in zebrafish ovaries.
source: Similar cysts were also observed in zebrafish ovaries (Marlow and Mullins, 2008; Beer and Draper, 2013; Bertho et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations on zebrafish oogenesis.

claim: Lei and Spradling, 2013a overcame the problem of analyzing cyst products by sparsely lineage marking individual migrating PGCs at E10.5.
source: Lei and Spradling, 2013a overcame this problem in mouse oogenesis by sparsely lineage marking individual migrating Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs) at E10.5, just as they were reaching the fetal ovary.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach used in a cited study.

claim: Lineage marking usually caused just one founder germ cell per ovary to be labeled, which produced one initial cyst of about 30 cells.
source: This usually caused just one founder germ cell per ovary to be labeled, which produced one initial cyst of about 30 cells.
evidence: This describes the result of the lineage marking experiment.

claim: About 4–6 labeled germ cells from the clone survived to become oocytes within 4–6 individual primordial follicles over 10 days.
source: Over the ensuing 10 days, about 4–6 labeled germ cells from the clone survived to become oocytes within 4–6 individual primordial follicles.
evidence: This describes the outcome of the lineage marking experiment.

claim: The initial cyst first fragmented into about 4–6 smaller derivative cysts by the time of meiotic onset, possibly in a programmed manner.
source: Closer study showed that the initial cyst first fragmented into about 4–6 smaller derivative cysts by the time of meiotic onset, possibly in a programmed manner (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Each derivative cyst specifies one oocyte with the remaining cells functioning as nurse cells that turn over by the time primordial follicles finish forming around P5.
source: This suggested that each derivative cyst specifies one oocyte with the remaining cells functioning as NCs that turn over by the time primordial follicles finish forming around P5.
evidence: This is an inference from the lineage marking data.

claim: The existence of vertebrate female germline cysts became clear, but their functional importance remained controversial.
source: While the existence of vertebrate female germline cysts became clear, their functional importance remained controversial.
evidence: This describes the state of the field at a particular time.

claim: Mutation of Tex14 disrupted IB stability and caused male sterility, but females continued to produce fertile eggs in reduced numbers.
source: Mutation of Tex14, encoding an important IB component and putative kinase known to function in cytokinesis, disrupted IB stability and caused male sterility, but females continued to produce fertile eggs in reduced numbers (Greenbaum et al., 2009; Greenbaum et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing Tex14 mutant phenotypes.

claim: A favored viewpoint was that unlike Drosophila, female vertebrate cysts are not essential, lack nurse cells, do not transfer organelles but simply produce uniform oogonial cells that either die or become oocytes.
source: A favored viewpoint remained that unlike Drosophila, female vertebrate cysts are not essential, lack NCs, do not transfer organelles but simply produce uniform oogonial cells that either die or became oocytes (Kloc et al., 2004a).
evidence: This describes a hypothesis that was later shown to be incorrect.

claim: Mouse ovarian cysts contain nurse cells and an oocyte.
source: However, ongoing studies of the mouse showed that this view is incorrect. Cyst cells in each of the smaller cysts derived from a PGC, when lineage marked, could be seen to consist of NCs and an oocyte (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from lineage marking studies, illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Organelles begin to move and accumulate in just one of the connected cells in mouse cysts.
source: Organelles begin to move and accumulate in just one of the connected cells (Lei and Spradling, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing organelle movement.

claim: The transferring cells become reduced in size, while the receiving cell grows and gradually takes on the appearance of an oocyte as the transferred centrosomes and organelles build up in its cytoplasm.
source: The transferring cells become reduced in size, while the receiving cell grows and gradually takes on the appearance of an oocyte as the transferred centrosomes and organelles build up in its cytoplasm.
evidence: This describes the morphological changes during organelle transfer.

claim: The distinct nature of nurse cells and oocytes was revealed by their cell type-specific patterns of gene expression even while they remain connected.
source: The distinct nature of NCs and oocytes was further revealed by their cell type-specific patterns of gene expression even while they remain connected (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: After transfer, mouse nurse cells turn over using a novel pathway of programmed cell death termed 'developmental cell death' rather than apoptosis.
source: After transfer, the NCs turn over, but they use a novel pathway of programmed cell death originally characterized in Drosophila termed 'developmental cell death' (Mondragon et al., 2019; Lebo and McCall, 2021) rather than apoptosis (Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the cell death pathway.

claim: Mouse cysts contain nurse cells and transfer most of their cytoplasm, centrosomes, and other organelles to an oocyte.
source: Thus, mouse cysts contain NCs and transfer most of their cytoplasm, centrosomes, and other organelles to an oocyte.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the studies described.

claim: The fertility of Tex14-/- animals is not due to oocyte production in the absence of cysts but because cyst production continues in the absence of stable IBs.
source: Applying single germ cell lineage tracing to Tex14 mutant ovaries showed that the fertility of Tex14-/- animals is not due to oocyte production in the absence of cysts but because cyst production continues in the absence of stable IBs (Ikami et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing lineage tracing in Tex14 mutants.

claim: Without Tex14, cytokinesis still arrests, but due to IB instability, a reduced number of smaller cysts with a variety of structures are generated.
source: Without Tex14, cytokinesis still arrests, but due to IB instability, a reduced number of smaller cysts with a variety of structures are generated.
evidence: This describes the phenotype of Tex14 mutants.

claim: Some Tex14 mutant cysts become linked by membrane holes and still develop both cell types with nurse cells transferring cytoplasm to generate functional oocytes.
source: Some Tex14 mutant cysts become linked by membrane holes, like older normal cysts. These cysts still develop both cell types and NCs transfer cytoplasm to generate functional oocytes.
evidence: This describes the functional outcome in Tex14 mutants.

claim: The loss of Tex14 dramatically accelerates the timing of nurse cell organelle transfer.
source: Strikingly, the loss of Tex14 dramatically accelerates the timing of NC organelle transfer, suggesting that Tex14 controls the organelle transfer schedule (Ikami et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing Tex14 mutant phenotypes.

claim: Tex14 controls the organelle transfer schedule.
source: Strikingly, the loss of Tex14 dramatically accelerates the timing of NC organelle transfer, suggesting that Tex14 controls the organelle transfer schedule (Ikami et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference from the observed acceleration of transfer in Tex14 mutants.

claim: Loss of Tex14 alters and accelerates the onset of the normal spatial pattern of meiotic initiation.
source: Loss of Tex14 also alters and accelerates the onset of the normal spatial pattern of meiotic initiation (Soygur et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing Tex14 mutant phenotypes.

claim: Most germ cell organelles and cytoplasm are transferred to surviving oocytes prior to nurse cell death.
source: These insights provide a physiological explanation for the longstanding mystery of extensive germ cell loss during mouse fetal and early juvenile development (Tilly, 2001; Grive, 2020). Most germ cell organelles and cytoplasm are transferred to surviving oocytes prior to NC death (Figure 2C), so little biosynthetic investment and time are actually lost, while completed oocytes are highly stable (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 2C and provides an explanation for germ cell loss.

claim: Little biosynthetic investment and time are lost due to nurse cell transfer before death.
source: Most germ cell organelles and cytoplasm are transferred to surviving oocytes prior to NC death (Figure 2C), so little biosynthetic investment and time are actually lost, while completed oocytes are highly stable (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of transfer before death.

claim: Completed oocytes are highly stable.
source: Most germ cell organelles and cytoplasm are transferred to surviving oocytes prior to NC death (Figure 2C), so little biosynthetic investment and time are actually lost, while completed oocytes are highly stable (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D depicting long-term follicle stability.

claim: Starting at E14.5, every 2 days 5–6 of the labeled PGC daughters not destined to become oocytes begin to transfer their cytoplasm.
source: Starting at E14.5, every 2 days 5–6 of the labeled PGC daughters not destined to become oocytes begin to transfer their cytoplasm, causing them to shrink into small cell remnants, before commencing programmed cell death (Figure 2A; Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The first nurse cells that become 'activated' for cytoplasmic transfer tend to be located at the edges of the cyst and have few connections to other cells.
source: The first such NCs that become 'activated' for cytoplasmic transfer tend to be located at the edges of the cyst and have few connections to other cells.
evidence: This describes a spatial pattern of nurse cell activation.

claim: Later rounds of nurse cell activation move closer to the central cells with the most interconnections.
source: Later rounds move closer to the central cells with the most interconnections.
evidence: This describes the progression of nurse cell activation.

claim: Mouse nurse cell cytoplasmic dumping and cell death do not happen all at once, like in Drosophila, but are spread out over an approximately 10-day period.
source: Thus, mouse NC cytoplasmic dumping and cell death do not happen all at once, like in Drosophila, but are spread out over an approximately 10-day period.
evidence: This is a comparative observation between mouse and Drosophila.

claim: Immediately after cysts have formed by E14.5, both nurse cells and oocytes express largely the same genes.
source: Immediately after cysts have formed by E14.5, both NCs and oocytes express largely the same genes characterized in previous studies analyzing total female germ cells.
evidence: This describes gene expression patterns at E14.5.

claim: As the first nurse cells activate cytoplasmic transfer during leptotene/zygotene, their gene expression changes sufficiently to be separately characterized using scRNAseq.
source: However, as the first NCs activate cytoplasmic transfer during leptotene/zygotene, their gene expression changes sufficiently to be separately characterized using scRNAseq.
evidence: This describes changes in gene expression detectable by scRNAseq.

claim: The 'E14.5 NCs' contain strikingly less mRNA on average than the other leptotene/zygotene germ cells, confirming their nurse cell identity.
source: The 'E14.5 NCs' in these clusters contain strikingly less mRNA on average than the other leptotene/zygotene germ cells, confirming their NC identity.
evidence: This is a finding from scRNAseq analysis that confirms cell identity.

claim: Oocyte and unactivated nurse cell gene expression coincides from E14.5 to E18.5.
source: Oocyte and unactivated NC gene expression coincides from E14.5 to E18.5, and beginning in P1 pure oocyte clusters can be sequenced.
evidence: This describes the timing of gene expression divergence.

claim: Beginning in P1, pure oocyte clusters can be sequenced.
source: Oocyte and unactivated NC gene expression coincides from E14.5 to E18.5, and beginning in P1 pure oocyte clusters can be sequenced.
evidence: This describes when oocytes can be analyzed separately by scRNAseq.

claim: Nobox protein is expressed specifically in oocytes but not nurse cells at E18.5.
source: The oocyte (larger size and, mitochondria content), but not nurse cells, expresses Nobox (from Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and supported by a citation.

claim: In Nobox-/- animals, cysts do not breakdown completely like in wild type.
source: In Nobox-/- animals, cysts do not breakdown completely like in wild type (Rajkovic et al., 2004), suggesting that oocyte-specific Nobox expression within late cysts promotes normal breakdown, possibly by causing the oocyte to send transfer-promoting signals to its remaining NCs.
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing Nobox mutant phenotypes.

claim: Oocyte-specific Nobox expression within late cysts promotes normal breakdown, possibly by causing the oocyte to send transfer-promoting signals to its remaining nurse cells.
source: In Nobox-/- animals, cysts do not breakdown completely like in wild type (Rajkovic et al., 2004), suggesting that oocyte-specific Nobox expression within late cysts promotes normal breakdown, possibly by causing the oocyte to send transfer-promoting signals to its remaining NCs.
evidence: This is an inference from the Nobox mutant phenotype.

claim: Tex14 expression levels in activated nurse cells fall three- to fourfold at E14.5 and E16.5 relative to pro-oocytes.
source: Changes in the expression of Tex14 within activated NCs may also contribute to cytoplasmic transfer. Tex14 expression levels in activated NCs fall three- to fourfold at E14.5 and E16.5 relative to pro-oocytes (Table 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: Reduced levels of Tex14 may accelerate transfer in the affected nurse cells, consistent with Tex14's apparent role as a local transfer repressor.
source: Reduced levels of Tex14 may accelerate transfer in the affected NCs, consistent with Tex14's apparent role as a local transfer repressor (Ikami et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on Tex14 function and expression patterns.

claim: Par family polarity protein mRNAs are downregulated in activated nurse cells.
source: Par family polarity protein mRNAs, including those encoding Pard3, Pard3b, Pard6a, Pard6b, and Mark3, are also downregulated in activated NCs (Pard6b, Table 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: Reduced Par expression may destabilize the nurse cell cytoskeleton to facilitate cytoplasmic transfer into the oocyte.
source: Reduced Par expression may destabilize the NC cytoskeleton to facilitate cytoplasmic transfer into the oocyte.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the function of reduced Par expression.

claim: The Follistatin (Fst) gene is expressed about fourfold higher in activated E14.5 nurse cells than in pro-oocytes and unactivated nurse cells.
source: The Follistatin (Fst) gene encodes an activin signaling regulator that is expressed about fourfold higher in activated E14.5 NCs than in pro-oocytes and unactivated NCs (Table 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: In female FST288-only mice, cysts fail to breakdown on schedule, with breakdown prolonged by several days.
source: In female FST288-only mice, cysts fail to breakdown on schedule, with breakdown prolonged by several days.
evidence: This describes a phenotype from a cited study on Follistatin.

claim: Excess primordial follicles are generated in FST288-only mice that subsequently turn over rapidly, leading to premature ovarian failure.
source: Excess primordial follicles are generated that subsequently turn over rapidly, leading to premature ovarian failure.
evidence: This describes a phenotype from the Follistatin mutant study.

claim: E16.5 nurse cells upregulate (3×) the level of Follistatin-like 1.
source: Interestingly, E16.5 NCs (Table 1) upregulate (3×) the level of a closely related gene, Follistatin-like 1.
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: p27Kip1 (Cdkn1b) is upregulated 2.9-fold in wild type E14.5 nurse cells compared to other E14.5 germ cells.
source: Another gene promoting cyst breakdown is p27Kip1 (Cdkn1b) which is upregulated 2.9-fold in wild type E14.5 NCs compared to other E14.5 germ cells (Table 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: p27Kip1 mutation increases the number of primordial follicles that are formed.
source: p27Kip1 mutation increases the number of primordial follicles that are formed (Rajareddy et al., 2007) as well as the number of 'multi-oocyte' follicles (Pérez-Sanz et al., 2013); both phenotypes indicate that cysts in the mutant did not breakdown normally.
evidence: This is supported by citations describing p27Kip1 mutant phenotypes.

claim: p27Kip1 mutation increases the number of 'multi-oocyte' follicles.
source: p27Kip1 mutation increases the number of primordial follicles that are formed (Rajareddy et al., 2007) as well as the number of 'multi-oocyte' follicles (Pérez-Sanz et al., 2013); both phenotypes indicate that cysts in the mutant did not breakdown normally.
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing p27Kip1 mutant phenotypes.

claim: In p27Kip1 mutant animals, the excess and multi-oocyte follicles are defective, and few survive to produce offspring.
source: Like in Fst mutants, in p27Kip1 mutant animals, the excess and multi-oocyte follicles are defective, and few survive to produce offspring.
evidence: This describes the functional consequences of the p27Kip1 mutation.

claim: Both Fst and p27Kip1 are expressed at much higher levels in granulosa cells surrounding cysts than in their transferring nurse cells.
source: An important caveat is that both Fst and p27Kip1 are expressed at much higher levels in granulosa cells surrounding cysts than in their transferring NCs, indicating that these genes may promote cyst breakdown by acting in somatic cells.
evidence: This is an observation about gene expression patterns.

claim: Fst and p27Kip1 may promote cyst breakdown by acting in somatic cells.
source: An important caveat is that both Fst and p27Kip1 are expressed at much higher levels in granulosa cells surrounding cysts than in their transferring NCs, indicating that these genes may promote cyst breakdown by acting in somatic cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the expression pattern data.

claim: Oocytes develop in germline cysts within species from diverse phylogenetic groups stretching back to the beginning of animal life more than 500 million years ago.
source: The studies reviewed here show that oocytes develop in germline cysts within species from diverse phylogenetic groups stretching back to the beginning of animal life more than 500 million years ago.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative analysis presented.

claim: Conservation of a complex developmental pathway involving multiple cells of two cell types produced by a conserved stereotyped process is highly unusual.
source: Such conservation of a complex developmental pathway involving multiple cells of two cell types produced by a conserved stereotyped process is highly unusual and suggests that cysts serve an important purpose that has changed little over animal history.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the evolutionary significance of cyst conservation.

claim: Cysts serve an important purpose that has changed little over animal history.
source: Such conservation of a complex developmental pathway involving multiple cells of two cell types produced by a conserved stereotyped process is highly unusual and suggests that cysts serve an important purpose that has changed little over animal history.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed evolutionary conservation.

claim: Germ cells harbor systems that preserve their nuclear genomes.
source: Germ cells are well known to harbor systems that preserve their nuclear genomes (Bergero et al., 2021; Cao and Pocock, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations on genome preservation in germ cells.

claim: Germ cells utilize mechanisms that select for and preserve undamaged mitochondrial DNA.
source: They also utilize mechanisms that select for and preserve undamaged mitochondrial DNA (Lieber et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; review Cox et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations on mitochondrial DNA preservation.

claim: Meiosis is critically important for rejuvenation of cellular damage acquired during cellular aging in yeast.
source: Studies in yeast show that meiosis is critically important for rejuvenation of cellular damage acquired during cellular aging.
evidence: This is based on studies in yeast cited in the text.

claim: During yeast sporulation, potentially damaging materials such as protein aggregates, aberrant nuclear pores, and excised rDNA circles are excluded from the four spore products.
source: Of particular importance, during sporulation potentially damaging materials such as protein aggregates, aberrant nuclear pores, and excised rDNA circles are excluded from the four spore products, whose aging clock is concomitantly reset (Unal et al., 2011; Goodman et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations on yeast sporulation.

claim: The aging clock is reset in yeast spore products.
source: Of particular importance, during sporulation potentially damaging materials such as protein aggregates, aberrant nuclear pores, and excised rDNA circles are excluded from the four spore products, whose aging clock is concomitantly reset (Unal et al., 2011; Goodman et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations on yeast rejuvenation.

claim: Cysts are strong candidates to provide rejuvenation benefits to animal germlines in association with meiosis.
source: Cysts are strong candidates to provide similar benefits to animal germlines, also in association with meiosis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on analogy to yeast.

claim: Residual cytoplasm and organelles within nurse cells are destroyed by proteolysis and physically excluded from entering the oocyte.
source: Residual cytoplasm and organelles within NCs are destroyed by proteolysis and physically excluded from entering the oocyte.
evidence: This describes a mechanism of quality control in oogenesis.

claim: Oogenesis in cysts containing nurse cells may be a vitally important safety valve to prevent a multi-generational decline in oocyte quality.
source: Thus, rather than simply promoting oocyte growth, oogenesis in cysts containing NCs may be a vitally important safety valve to prevent a multi-generational decline in oocyte quality.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the function of cysts.

claim: Germ cells must continue to function in perpetuity, which makes defects more difficult to test.
source: Unlike somatic cells, which need only last one generation, germ cells must continue to function in perpetuity, which makes defects more difficult to test.
evidence: This is a logical statement about the unique requirements of germ cells.

claim: Many vertebrate and invertebrate oocytes contribute patterning information in the form of specified embryonic axes that guide early embryonic development.
source: Many vertebrate and invertebrate oocytes contribute not only rejuvenated cellular materials but also patterning information in the form of specified embryonic axes that guide early embryonic development.
evidence: This is a statement about oocyte contributions to development.

claim: Evo-Devo comparisons have revealed an underlying genetic similarity in how animal embryos, tissues, and their germ cells develop within different species.
source: Evo-Devo comparisons of genomes, genes, and developmental pathways have revealed an underlying genetic similarity in how animal embryos, tissues, and their germ cells develop within different species, consistent with evidence that animals constitute a monophyletic group stretching back to a common animal ancestor (Fierro-Constaín et al., 2017; De Robertis and Tejeda-Muñoz, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations on evolutionary developmental biology.

claim: Animals constitute a monophyletic group stretching back to a common animal ancestor.
source: Evo-Devo comparisons of genomes, genes, and developmental pathways have revealed an underlying genetic similarity in how animal embryos, tissues, and their germ cells develop within different species, consistent with evidence that animals constitute a monophyletic group stretching back to a common animal ancestor (Fierro-Constaín et al., 2017; De Robertis and Tejeda-Muñoz, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations on animal phylogeny.

claim: The germline cyst is the earliest conserved multicellular assembly on the developmental pathway of most major animal groups.
source: It is plausible to consider that the germline cyst, the earliest conserved multicellular assembly on the developmental pathway of most major animal groups, contributes to the oocyte's ability to launch embryonic development.
evidence: This is a characterization of the germline cyst's evolutionary position.

claim: The germline cyst may contribute to the oocyte's ability to launch embryonic development.
source: It is plausible to consider that the germline cyst, the earliest conserved multicellular assembly on the developmental pathway of most major animal groups, contributes to the oocyte's ability to launch embryonic development.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about cyst function.

claim: Oocytes are currently believed to contribute less patterning information to mouse and mammalian embryonic development than do the oocytes of other well-studied animals such as Drosophila and lower vertebrates.
source: Oocytes are currently believed to contribute less patterning information to mouse and mammalian embryonic development than do the oocytes of other well-studied animals such as Drosophila and lower vertebrates (Beddington and Robertson, 1999; Gardner and Davies, 2003; Innocenti et al., 2022), raising the question of whether patterning functions of cysts would be conserved in mammals.
evidence: This is supported by citations on mammalian development.

claim: The Balbiani body's position in the early follicle relative to the oocyte nucleus prefigures the animal/vegetal embryonic axis in diverse animal species including many vertebrates.
source: An organelle known as the Balbiani body has long been of interest in developmental biology because its position in the early follicle relative to the oocyte nucleus (known as the germinal vesicle - GV) prefigures the animal/vegetal embryonic axis in diverse animal species including many vertebrates (Figure 3A; Wilson, 1925).
evidence: This is supported by a historical citation and illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: A human Balbiani body was observed more than 100 years ago as a large oocyte organelle cluster centered around a 'cytocentrum' in primordial follicles.
source: A human Bb was observed more than 100 years ago as a large oocyte organelle cluster centered around a 'cytocentrum' in primordial follicles (Figure 3A and B; van der Stricht, 1923; Raven, 1961; Hertig, 1968; Kloc et al., 2004b).
evidence: This is supported by historical citations and illustrated in Figures 3A and B.

claim: Similar Balbiani body structures are found in mouse, Drosophila, Xenopus, zebrafish, and even in panoistic insects.
source: Similar Bb structures are found in mouse (Figure 3C; Pepling et al., 2007; Kloc et al., 2008), Drosophila (Mahowald and Strassheim, 1970), Xenopus (Kloc et al., 2004a), zebrafish (Elkouby et al., 2016), and even in panoistic insects (Tworzydlo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations across multiple species and illustrated in Figure 3C.

claim: The germline cyst contributes essentially to Balbiani body formation in Drosophila, mouse, and probably many other species.
source: The germline cyst contributes essentially to Bb formation in Drosophila (Cox and Spradling, 2003), mouse (Lei and Spradling, 2016), and probably many other species.
evidence: This is supported by citations and extrapolated to other species.

claim: Before the onset of meiosis or Balbiani body appearance, the germline cyst's polarity has been established.
source: Before the onset of meiosis or Bb appearance, the germline cyst's polarity has been established, and at meiotic onset, this polarity mediates MT-dependent transport of materials that specify the oocyte(s) and begin to generate a Bb(s).
evidence: This describes the timing of polarity establishment.

claim: At meiotic onset, cyst polarity mediates MT-dependent transport of materials that specify the oocyte(s) and begin to generate a Balbiani body.
source: Before the onset of meiosis or Bb appearance, the germline cyst's polarity has been established, and at meiotic onset, this polarity mediates MT-dependent transport of materials that specify the oocyte(s) and begin to generate a Bb(s).
evidence: This describes the function of cyst polarity.

claim: During zygotene to dictyate meiotic stages, centrosomes and other organelles undergo MT-dependent transport from nurse cells to the oocyte.
source: During zygotene to dictyate meiotic stages, centrosomes and other organelles undergo MT-dependent transport from NCs to the oocyte (Cox and Spradling, 2003; Cox and Spradling, 2006; Lei and Spradling, 2016; Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing organelle transport.

claim: In mouse, the transported centrosomes coalesce in the oocyte and generate the cytocentrum consisting of pericentriolar material surrounded by Golgi membranes.
source: In mouse, the transported centrosomes coalesce in the oocyte and generate the cytocentrum (Figure 3D and E) consisting of pericentriolar material surrounded by Golgi membranes (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figures 3D, E, and F.

claim: The cytocentrum nucleates a large MT aster on which oocyte organelles associate to form the Balbiani body.
source: The cytocentrum, whose formation requires tubulin gene function (Niu and Spradling, 2022), nucleates a large MT aster (Figure 3G) on which oocyte organelles associate to form the Bb (Lei and Spradling, 2016; Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 3G.

claim: Cytocentrum formation requires tubulin gene function.
source: The cytocentrum, whose formation requires tubulin gene function (Niu and Spradling, 2022), nucleates a large MT aster (Figure 3G) on which oocyte organelles associate to form the Bb (Lei and Spradling, 2016; Niu and Spradling, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Microtubules play critical roles in Balbiani body production by transporting organelles to the oocyte from nurse cells, forming the cytocentrum, and organizing oocyte organelles into a characteristic Balbiani body structure on nucleated MTs.
source: Thus, MTs play critical roles in Bb production by transporting organelles to the oocyte from NCs, forming the cytocentrum, and organizing oocyte organelles into a characteristic Bb structure on nucleated MTs.
evidence: This is a summary of MT functions in Bb formation.

claim: MT disruption at any stage abolishes Balbiani body formation.
source: MT disruption at any stage in this process abolishes Bb formation.
evidence: This describes the essential role of MTs.

claim: In Drosophila, the number of mitochondria in the Balbiani body can be manipulated over a wide range by mutating MT motors or the two Milton mitochondrial transport adaptor protein isoforms expressed in oocytes.
source: In Drosophila, the number of mitochondria in the Bb can even be manipulated over a wide range by mutating MT motors or the two Milton mitochondrial transport adaptor protein isoforms expressed in oocytes (Cox and Spradling, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing genetic manipulation experiments.

claim: Nurse cell centriole migration to the oocyte prior to follicle formation was originally described in Drosophila.
source: NC centriole migration to the oocyte prior to follicle formation was originally described in Drosophila (Mahowald and Strassheim, 1970).
evidence: This is supported by a historical citation.

claim: Nurse cell centrioles move along the fusome and arrive at the oocyte as the follicle begins to form at the onset of stage 1.
source: NC centrioles move along the fusome and arrive at the oocyte as the follicle begins to form at the onset of stage 1 then rapidly move to the posterior where they aggregate as revealed by EM (Mahowald and Strassheim, 1970) and by gamma-tubulin staining (Grieder et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing centriole migration.

claim: The aggregated centrioles may represent a Drosophila analog of the cytocentrum.
source: The aggregated centrioles may represent a Drosophila analog of the cytocentrum.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the relationship between structures.

claim: As stage 1 continues in Drosophila, the posterior MTOC forms and the Balbiani body coalesces.
source: As stage 1 continues, the posterior MTOC forms (Theurkauf et al., 1993) and the Bb coalesces (Cox and Spradling, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing developmental timing.

claim: The Drosophila posterior MTOC is likely a non-centriolar MTOC.
source: The functional role of centriole migration in Drosophila for generating the posterior MTOC has remained uncertain, and this MTOC is likely non-centriolar MTOC (ncMTOC; Bolívar et al., 2001; Nashchekin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Disruption of the centriolar replication factor SAS-4 eliminates centrioles but does not block oogenesis.
source: Moreover, disruption of the centriolar replication factor SAS-4 eliminates centrioles but does not block oogenesis (Stevens et al., 2007), possibly because peri-centriolar material sufficient for posterior MTOC formation is still available in the oocyte (Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing SAS-4 mutant phenotypes.

claim: Peri-centriolar material sufficient for posterior MTOC formation may still be available in the oocyte when centrioles are eliminated.
source: Moreover, disruption of the centriolar replication factor SAS-4 eliminates centrioles but does not block oogenesis (Stevens et al., 2007), possibly because peri-centriolar material sufficient for posterior MTOC formation is still available in the oocyte (Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the SAS-4 mutant phenotype, supported by a citation.

claim: Centriole migration may have functions beyond MTOC formation.
source: Centriole migration may have other functions as well (Braun et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation suggesting additional functions.

claim: Targeted alteration of the APC/C-specific E2 ligase Vihar blocked centriole migration by causing premature polo kinase degradation and centriole destabilization in the oocyte.
source: Centriole migration was blocked by targeted alteration of the APC/C-specific E2 ligase Vihar, which caused premature polo kinase degradation and centriole destabilization in the oocyte without altering the fusome.
evidence: This describes a genetic manipulation and its effects.

claim: Without centriole migration, the oocyte still formed but could not be maintained due to ectopic MT nucleation in nurse cells that probably interfered with NC to oocyte transport.
source: Without centriole migration, the oocyte still formed but could not be maintained due to ectopic MT nucleation in NCs that probably interfered with NC to oocyte transport.
evidence: This describes the phenotype when centriole migration is blocked.

claim: Relocating nurse cell centrioles to the oocyte may help establish and maintain a stable MT cytoskeleton in both cell types.
source: Thus, relocating NC centrioles to the oocyte may help establish and maintain a stable MT cytoskeleton in both cell types.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the function of centriole migration.

claim: The fact that centrosome/centriole migration has been conserved between Drosophila and mouse argues strongly that this process serves an important function.
source: The fact that centrosome/centriole migration has been conserved between Drosophila and mouse argues strongly that this process serves an important function.
evidence: This is an inference from evolutionary conservation.

claim: Centrosome/centriole migrations act as a switch to activate new ncMTOC formation that organizes the Balbiani body and defines the Bb-GV axis that presages the Drosophila a/p axis.
source: We suggest that these migrations act as a switch to activate new ncMTOC formation that organizes the Bb and defines the Bb-GV axis that presages the Drosophila a/p axis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The mouse cytocentrum activates a powerful ncMTOC on cytocentrum-associated Golgi membranes.
source: Based on its size and shape, we propose that the mouse cytocentrum activates a powerful ncMTOC on cytocentrum-associated Golgi membranes (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors, illustrated in Figures 3G and H.

claim: Drosophila centriole migration may activate ncMTOC activity at the oocyte posterior, where Golgi elements cluster.
source: Likewise, Drosophila centriole migration may activate ncMTOC activity at the oocyte posterior, where Golgi elements cluster (Cox and Spradling, 2003).
evidence: This is a hypothesis by analogy to mouse, supported by a citation.

claim: A variety of cells and fibroblast cell lines have a Golgi-associated ncMTOC in addition to a centriolar MTOC.
source: A variety of cells and fibroblast cell lines in addition to a centriolar MTOC have a second, Golgi-associated ncMTOC (Rios, 2014; Valenzuela et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations on Golgi-associated MTOCs.

claim: Golgi-nucleated MTOCs utilize Cdk5rap2 and TPPP family members.
source: Golgi-nucleated MTOCs utilize Cdk5rap2, which binds to the gamma-tubulin ring complex, as well as tubulin polymerization promoting protein (TPPP) family members.
evidence: This describes molecular components of Golgi MTOCs.

claim: Both Cdk5rap2 and TPPP3 are expressed in dictyate mouse oocytes based on scRNAseq.
source: Both Cdk5rap2 and TPPP3 are expressed in dictyate mouse oocytes based on scRNAseq.
evidence: This is based on scRNAseq data.

claim: CAMSAP proteins bind and stabilize Golgi-nucleated MT minus ends, including the mouse oocyte-expressed CAMSAP1.
source: Additionally, CAMSAP proteins bind and stabilize Golgi-nucleated MT minus ends, including the mouse oocyte-expressed CAMSAP1, a Patronin ortholog.
evidence: This describes a molecular mechanism and expression pattern.

claim: In cultured cells, loss of the centriolar MTOC can cause Golgi-dependent MT nucleation to become predominant.
source: In cultured cells, loss of the centriolar MTOC can cause Golgi-dependent MT nucleation to become predominant (Gavilan et al., 2018; Martin and Akhmanova, 2018; Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations on MTOC compensation.

claim: In Xenopus and zebrafish, germ granules and mRNAs become localized within the oocyte Balbiani body throughout stage 1 after follicle formation.
source: Studies in Xenopus (Kloc et al., 2004b; King et al., 2005) and zebrafish (Jamieson-Lucy and Mullins, 2019) showed that germ granules and mRNAs become localized within the oocyte Bb throughout stage 1 after follicle formation.
evidence: This is supported by citations on Xenopus and zebrafish.

claim: Germ granules and mRNAs are subsequently transported to the vegetal pole cortex and undergo subsequent waves of vegetal or animal pole localization in Xenopus and zebrafish.
source: They are subsequently transported to the vegetal pole cortex and undergo subsequent waves of vegetal or animal pole localization, where they persist and play essential roles in oocyte patterning and germ-cell formation in the early embryo.
evidence: This describes developmental processes in Xenopus and zebrafish.

claim: Localized germ granules and mRNAs play essential roles in oocyte patterning and germ-cell formation in the early embryo.
source: They are subsequently transported to the vegetal pole cortex and undergo subsequent waves of vegetal or animal pole localization, where they persist and play essential roles in oocyte patterning and germ-cell formation in the early embryo.
evidence: This describes functional roles of localized materials.

claim: Some mRNAs initially deposited at the vegetal pole are later reoriented to define the future dorsal-ventral axis.
source: Some of the mRNAs initially deposited at the vegetal pole are later reoriented to define the future dorsal-ventral (d/v) axis (reviewed in Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Colozza and De Robertis, 2014; King et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by review citations.

claim: A similar sequence of events takes place in Drosophila oocytes on a greatly accelerated time scale.
source: A similar sequence of events takes place in Drosophila oocytes on a greatly accelerated time scale, perhaps consistent with the much more rapid development of Drosophila oocytes generally.
evidence: This is a comparative observation.

claim: Oskar and orb/CPEB mRNAs move along the fusome and briefly associate with the Balbiani body as it initially forms in Drosophila.
source: Oskar and orb/CPEB mRNAs move along the fusome and briefly associate with the Bb as it initially forms, before moving to the oocyte posterior (Cox and Spradling, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation on mRNA localization in Drosophila.

claim: Some originally posterior mRNAs such as gurken mRNA are later reoriented to establish the d/v axis in Drosophila.
source: Like in Xenopus, some originally posterior mRNAs such as gurken mRNA are later reoriented to establish the d/v axis, a process that in Drosophila occurs long after the Bb has dispersed and that involves further changes in the MT cytoskeleton, including new ncMTOCs (Milas and Telley, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation on Drosophila axis specification.

claim: The buckyball gene is essential for Balbiani body persistence and for oocyte patterning in zebrafish.
source: Genetic analysis of Bb formation in zebrafish identified the buckyball gene, which does not affect initial Bb formation, but is essential for Bb persistence and for oocyte patterning (Marlow and Mullins, 2008; Elkouby and Mullins, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations on buckyball function.

claim: Buckyball and Xvelo are predicted to be intrinsically disordered proteins.
source: Buckyball and Xvelo, its Xenopus ortholog (Claussen and Pieler, 2004; Boke et al., 2016), are predicted to be intrinsically disordered proteins (Brangwynne et al., 2009; Han et al., 2012; Seydoux, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations on protein structure predictions.

claim: Formation of phase-separated compartments might stabilize the initial Balbiani body, allowing it to persist for long periods.
source: Formation of phase-separated compartments might stabilize the initial Bb, allowing it to persist for long periods and carry out its multiple functions in mRNA and germ granule localization.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about Bb stabilization.

claim: The strong conservation in mouse oocytes of events associated with oocyte polarization suggests that these processes continue to play a significant role.
source: The strong conservation in mouse oocytes of events associated with oocyte polarization, including development within a cyst, centrosome transfer from NCs, and centrosome assembly into a cytocentrum and Bb that defines a Bb-GV axis, suggests that these processes continue to play a significant role.
evidence: This is an inference from evolutionary conservation.

claim: Efforts to identify localized mRNAs arising in Bb-stage oocytes that move to the oocyte cortex have not been successful.
source: Efforts to identify localized mRNAs arising in Bb-stage oocytes that move to the oocyte cortex have not been successful.
evidence: This is a statement about unsuccessful research efforts.

claim: Viviparity significantly delays embryonic development and patterning relative to non-eutherians, in favor of extraembryonic tissue growth needed to establish a maternal trophic connection.
source: Many challenges in comparing mammalian oocyte development to those in other groups are due to viviparity, which significantly delays embryonic development and patterning relative to non-eutherians, in favor of extraembryonic tissue growth needed to establish a maternal trophic connection (O'Farrell et al., 2004; Maltepe and Fisher, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations on mammalian development.

claim: A new pathway may have evolved to transduce into the embryo the long-conserved patterning role for the polarized oocyte.
source: It is plausible that a new pathway evolved to transduce into the embryo the long-conserved patterning role for the polarized oocyte.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about evolutionary adaptation.

claim: Depletion of SCMC components causes maternal infertility due to embryo arrest at cleavage stages.
source: Depletion of SCMC components causes maternal infertility due to embryo arrest at cleavage stages (Li et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation on SCMC function.

claim: Floped localizes to the apical part of the cell and cell cortex and is involved in establishing apical/basal polarity.
source: One SCMC component, Floped, localizes to the apical part of the cell and cell cortex and is involved in establishing apical/basal polarity.
evidence: This describes the localization and function of Floped.

claim: Padi6 contributes to the cytoskeletal organization and is a component of 'cytoplasmic lattices' that form in the oocyte.
source: Another Padi6 contributes to the cytoskeletal organization and is a component of 'cytoplasmic lattices' that form in the oocyte (Capco and McGaughey, 1986; Esposito et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations on Padi6 function.

claim: Cytoplasmic lattices persist in the early embryo.
source: These structures persist in the early embryo and might transmit patterning information, although such a connection acting beyond the 2cell stage has not been demonstrated.
evidence: This describes the persistence of cytoplasmic lattices.

claim: The mammalian oocyte may imprint embryonic pattern information onto a stable extracellular structure such as the zona pellucida.
source: Another possibility is that the mammalian oocyte imprints embryonic pattern information onto a stable extracellular structure such as the zona pellucida (ZP) lying just outside the oocyte surface.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about pattern information transfer.

claim: The Drosophila oocyte transduces the oocyte dorsal/ventral axis to the fly embryo through signals to follicle cells that alter the structure of the vitelline membrane.
source: The Drosophila oocyte carries out such a strategy to transduce the oocyte dorsal/ventral (d/v) axis to the fly embryo (review: Stein and Stevens, 2014; Merkle et al., 2020). Germ cell signals to the follicle cells cause them to alter the structure of the vitelline membrane that lies just outside the oocyte plasma membrane, with d/v asymmetry.
evidence: This is supported by review citations on Drosophila axis specification.

claim: Vitelline membrane signals are read out after fertilization by proteolysis, bind to oocyte surface receptors, and establish the d/v axis in the Drosophila embryo.
source: These signals are later read out after fertilization by proteolysis, bind to oocyte surface receptors, and establish the d/v axis in the embryo (see: Nüsslein-Volhard, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation on Drosophila development.

claim: Mouse extraembryonic endoderm plays a major role in patterning the inner cell mass by migrating anteriorly and forming the anterior visceral endoderm.
source: Mouse extraembryonic endoderm (EE) represents a possible target since these cells plays a major role in patterning the inner cell mass by migrating anteriorly and forming the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE; reviewed in Stower and Srinivas, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a review citation on mouse development.

claim: Gene expression in AVE cells establishes an a/p axis in the epiblast.
source: Gene expression in AVE cells establishes an a/p axis in the epiblast.
evidence: This describes a developmental mechanism.

claim: Patterning information from the Balbiani body-containing early mouse oocyte may be transferred locally to extracellular matrix and forming zona pellucida.
source: We propose that patterning information from the Balbinai body-containing early mouse oocyte is transferred locally to extracellular matrix (ECM) and forming zona pellucida.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: There is extensive evidence of secretory activity from the Bb-associated Golgi membranes of mouse oocytes at P4.
source: There is extensive evidence of secretory activity from the Bb-associated Golgi membranes of mouse oocytes at P4 (Lei and Spradling, 2016) and molecular evidence that granulosa cells synthesize ECM proteins at this time (Niu and Spradling, 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by citations on secretory activity.

claim: Granulosa cells synthesize ECM proteins at P4.
source: There is extensive evidence of secretory activity from the Bb-associated Golgi membranes of mouse oocytes at P4 (Lei and Spradling, 2016) and molecular evidence that granulosa cells synthesize ECM proteins at this time (Niu and Spradling, 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Asymmetries established in the zona pellucida may be read out in the embryo and program EE cells to become AVE precursors that establish the embryonic a/p axis.
source: It is plausible that asymmetries established in the ZP are read out in the embryo and program a limited number of precursor EE cells in the early embryo to become AVE precursors that establish the embryonic a/p axis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about pattern information transfer.

claim: The ancient connection between the Bb-GV axis and the a/p axis may not have been lost at the time of eutherian evolution but modified to continue to provide its long-conserved role.
source: Regardless of exact mechanistic details, the ancient connection between the Bb-GV axis and the a/p axis may not have been lost at the time of eutherian evolution but modified to continue to provide its long-conserved role.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about evolutionary conservation.

claim: We would be ignorant today of the fundamental role of cysts in vertebrate and mammalian oogenesis had not studies of a wide range of organisms been supported and valued, especially of invertebrates and insects.
source: We would be ignorant today of the fundamental role of cysts in vertebrate and mammalian oogenesis had not studies of a wide range of organisms been supported and valued, especially of invertebrates and insects.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of comparative biology.

claim: Evolution has conserved much of animal biology.
source: Because evolution has conserved so much of animal biology, what matters in basic science is to study processes in systems that are favorable to advancing our understanding, while the particular species or group analyzed is intrinsically of less importance.
evidence: This is a general statement about evolutionary conservation.
